title: Spillover Effects and Freemium Strategy in the Mobile App Market
authors: Yiting Deng; Anja Lambrecht; Yongdong Liu
near_miss_reason: Free-version launches occur at app-specific dates, but every reported column is a stacked matched-group design: each freemium app and its matched control apps form a group (treatment_id), the data are re-indexed to a 29-day event window (date index, a single treat_date for all groups), and regressions absorb app-within-group (cluster_id) and group-by-date (cluster_date) FE. Every TWFE column also includes lagged time-varying regressors (l_top10..l_top, l_price, l_ln_nrating = lagged log cumulative ratings, l_if_rated, l_rating). Treated-only columns (Table 5) have no time FE or control units. Stacked-only, so excluded under the 5b/Nov 1 coding rule (not a controls-only near-miss).
eligible_reason: Stacked-only design (group x date and app-in-group FE in an event-time-aligned window) with lagged time-varying controls in every column; no unstacked unit + calendar-time TWFE specification.
design_notes: Stata reghdfe/xtreg (freemium_code.do). Main Table 6: reghdfe ln_dnrating treat_after + lagged controls if abs(date-treat_date)<=14 (or 7), absorb(i.cluster_date i.cluster_id), cluster cluster_id. Tables 8-12: subsamples and treat_after interactions with app characteristics (rating, napp, features). Table 7: ranking and Google Play versions with the same structure. Figure 4: event study ib13.treat_ndays with the same FE and controls. matching_freemium_apps_full_script.py builds the matched control groups.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 774 freemium apps with app-specific launch dates in calendar time, but the shipped data are event-time aligned (date 1-29, treat_date constant) so calendar dates are not recoverable.
data_files_note: AppMonsta data under NDA. Readme section 3: shipped samples keep a random half of freemium apps with their matched controls, re-index app IDs, and add uniform noise in [-0.25 sd, 0.25 sd] to every continuous variable (Google download data: 0.1% sample with the same noise).
data_provenance_note: Random half of groups plus additive noise on continuous variables (outcome ln_dnrating included).
software_notes: Stata; Python for matching; R for Figure 2
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text or PDF). Stacked matched-group DiD with lagged controls; data disguised with noise.
